name: The Estates
summary: Auction-driven real-estate game where players stack colored cubes into towers to control row values and score positive or negative points.
rules_text: Each player starts with $12M in a closed economy. On your turn you choose one available component - a colored value cube, a roof, a row-length contract, a cancel cube, or the mayor - and auction it once around the table. Bids rise once only. As auctioneer you then either keep the item and pay the high bidder their bid, or sell it and take their money. Cubes are placed on a grid: alone in an empty lot or stacked on another lot. The color of the top cube owns the whole tower and the owner takes that color's deed if first. A row is complete when every lot has a building and a roof; contracts lengthen or shorten rows. When two rows are complete the game ends. Completed rows score face values plus roofs positively; incomplete rows score negatively. Mayor doubles one row. Most money plus building points wins; money kept aside also scores.
rating_reason: Auction and bidding with bluffing, turn-based, arithmetic scoring
reasons: scope: spatial_board: out of scope by decision: the game depends on a spatial board (a grid, map, movement or adjacency)
